clue.text: Astronomical measure taking pages in work on hydrogen filters, possibly

indicators.note: the wordplay 'takes' the next item in, holding it inside its own letters
in a down-free across reading, one item placed 'on' another simply follows straight after it

parts.note: to do is to work

indicators.note: 'possibly' says the letters before it are only one way of arranging what is meant, so they must be rearranged

parts.note: pp is the standard abbreviation for pages
H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen, joined to the word filters as the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: An astronomer measuring something while working on filters for hydrogen light, flipping through pages of notes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Filters' looks like a noun or verb about optics, but with hydrogen's symbol it is the fodder, and 'possibly' turns it round; the pages go in right after the work.
explanation.definitionFit: The Doppler shift of light, its redshift or blueshift, is used by astronomers to measure how fast stars and galaxies move.

clue.text: Limitations to dialogue, as it happens, precluding one search

indicators.note: the limits of a word are its two ends, so only its first and last letters are kept

parts.note: the two boundary letters of dialogue

indicators.note: to preclude is to shut out, so the item named next is removed

parts.note: a broadcast shown live goes out as it happens
the Roman numeral for one, taken out

explanation.surface: A scriptwriter feeling the limits of live dialogue while searching for words.
explanation.walkthrough: Broadcasting jargon helps here: a show that goes out as it happens is live.
explanation.definitionFit: To delve is to dig deep or investigate thoroughly, a fair synonym for search as a verb.

clue.text: Unusual things father noticed about woman and blokes pursuing love

indicators.note: the father figure is seen around what follows, so his letters enclose it

parts.note: an informal word for father

indicators.note: to pursue is to come after, so the blokes are placed behind the love

parts.note: hen is informal for a woman, as in a hen party
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O
blokes are men

explanation.surface: A father spotting his daughter out with a group of men in love, which strikes him as odd.
explanation.walkthrough: The father's two letters enclose all of the woman, love and blokes together.
explanation.definitionFit: Phenomena are remarkable or extraordinary occurrences, so unusual things is a fair plural match.

clue.text: Add humour to difficult situation, heading off doom almost entirely

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, and it is taken off

parts.note: a plight is a difficult situation

indicators.note: almost the whole word is used, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: one's doom is one's end

explanation.surface: Advice to bring some jokes into a grim, doom-laden situation.
explanation.walkthrough: PLIGHT loses its first letter and END its last, leaving LIGHT and EN.
explanation.definitionFit: To lighten a mood or a piece of writing is to make it less serious, which adding humour does.

clue.text: Survivors beginning to read extracts, needing to forget one island

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of read

indicators.note: forgetting something leaves it out, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: to elicit information is to extract it
I stands for island; only one of the two in the word goes

explanation.surface: Survivors of a shipwreck start reading out passages, but forget one island they were on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One island' is a single I: the word for extracts has two, and only one is forgotten.
explanation.definitionFit: Relicts are organisms or things surviving from an earlier period after others have died out.

clue.text: Sound of steam-train initially cut — something done on board?

indicators.note: the initial letter of the word is cut away, leaving the rest

parts.note: a steam engine chuffs as it moves

explanation.surface: The puffing of a steam engine cut short, with the board suggesting a train timetable or a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: In draughts (checkers), to huff is to remove an opponent's piece that failed to make a compulsory capture; 'board' means the game board, not boarding a train.
explanation.definitionFit: A huff is a move made in the game of draughts, so it is literally an action carried out on the playing board.

clue.text: Books, in current form, adopted by generous visionary

indicators.note: something adopted is taken in, so these letters go inside the next word

parts.note: a fat cheque or fat salary is a generous one
NT, the New Testament, is a set of books
as is means in its present state

explanation.surface: A generous patron taking on books in their present form, as a dreamer might.
explanation.walkthrough: FAT holds NT and AS IS: FA + NT + ASIS + T.
explanation.definitionFit: A fantasist is someone who lives in fantasies, a dreamer, which is one sense of visionary.

clue.text: Away to finish revolt

parts.note: off means away, as in going off
to end is to finish

explanation.surface: A rebel slipping away to bring the uprising to a close.
explanation.walkthrough: Revolt reads as a noun for an uprising, but here it is the verb meaning to disgust.
explanation.definitionFit: To revolt someone is to disgust or upset them, which is what it means to offend.

clue.text: Greek island runs hot with poems by Sappho?

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
H for hot, as on a tap
Sappho wrote lyric poems, odes being one example; the question mark flags this

explanation.surface: A Greek island with hot weather and a tradition of Sappho's poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: Sappho actually came from Lesbos, which is what the surface wants you to write; the island here is built from parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhodes is the largest of the Dodecanese islands in the Aegean Sea, belonging to Greece.

clue.text: Fine drink, with second consumed? Not so

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

indicators.note: a thing consumed is swallowed inside, so this letter goes into the drink

parts.note: ale is a drink
S is short for second

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether fine wine was drunk in a second, and gets a denial.
explanation.walkthrough: The second goes inside the drink, not after it, and the fine stands in front of both.
explanation.definitionFit: Something false is untrue, so 'not so' is a short way of saying it is not the case.

clue.text: Flapper beginning to dabble in sport? No great amount

indicators.note: the letter goes in, placed inside the sport's name

parts.note: golf is a sport

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, which is all that is kept

parts.note: the first letter of dabble
an inch is a small measure, nothing much

explanation.surface: A 1920s flapper girl dabbling in a sport, though not very much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flapper' suggests a jazz-age young woman, but it is a cryptic word for a bird, which flaps its wings.
explanation.definitionFit: A goldfinch is a small songbird, and any bird is something that flaps its wings in flight.

clue.text: Fixed gaze from detective not favouring discretion

parts.note: a private eye is a detective
con means against, as in pros and cons
tact is discretion in dealing with people

explanation.surface: A detective's hard stare that does nothing to suggest discretion.
explanation.definitionFit: Eye contact is two people looking straight into each other's eyes, a steady look held between them.

clue.text: Tough vegetable, not cooked at first

indicators.note: not tells us the selected letter must be absent from the vegetable

parts.note: chard is a leafy green vegetable

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: the opening letter of cooked

explanation.surface: A vegetable left tough because it was not cooked first.
explanation.walkthrough: CHARD minus the C from the start of cooked.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard and tough are synonyms, describing something firm and resistant or a difficult task.

clue.text: Observe Germany is leading European research centre

indicators.note: leading means going in front, so these pieces come before the research centre

parts.note: D is the international vehicle code for Germany (Deutschland)
taken as written
CERN is the European particle physics laboratory near Geneva

explanation.surface: A note that Germany is out in front at Europe's chief physics laboratory.
explanation.definitionFit: To discern is to perceive or make out, which is a sense of observe.

clue.text: What's best with tart?

indicators.note: with means alongside, so the two pieces are set next to one another

parts.note: tart means sharp-tasting, acidic
the cream is the best part, as in the cream of the crop

explanation.surface: Asking what goes best with a fruit tart, a sweet pastry dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: the dessert reading expects plain cream, but read 'tart' as an adjective and the pieces run in reverse clue order.
explanation.definitionFit: Sour cream is cream soured with bacteria, so it is the cream of milk combined with a tart taste.

clue.text: Leader of Spain is repeatedly collaring European wets

indicators.note: to collar is to grab round the neck, so these letters close around the next one

parts.note: the leading letter of Spain followed by is, the pair written out twice
E is short for European

explanation.surface: A Spanish leader repeatedly grabbing Europe's weaklings by the collar.
explanation.walkthrough: The E slips in just before the final letter. Wets is British slang for feeble, spineless people.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a wet is a feeble, ineffectual person, and sissies are weak or timid people.

clue.text: Poor illumination, with line disconnected, offering some constraint

parts.note: skint is British slang for broke, having no money

indicators.note: a line disconnected is cut off, so the letter for line is removed

parts.note: light is illumination
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A household so poor the power line was cut off, leaving them with only dim light.
explanation.walkthrough: Skint is everyday British slang for penniless. LIGHT loses its L to become IGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Skintight clothing fits closely and so holds the body in, providing a degree of restriction.

clue.text: German design centre's expression of annoyance about University linking to Australia

indicators.note: linking to means joined on, so the next piece is attached at the end
about means around, so the exclamation goes round the letter that follows

parts.note: bah is an exclamation of irritation
U is short for university
Aus is the abbreviation for Australia

explanation.surface: A German design school irritated about a university partnership with Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'German design centre's' read as a possessive, but the 's is just 'is' linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bauhaus was the influential German school of art, architecture and design founded by Walter Gropius in 1919.

clue.text: American composer, person almost enthralling both sides

indicators.note: to enthral is to hold captive, so the letters are held inside
almost the whole word is used, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: a being is a person, as in human being
the two sides are right and left, R and L

explanation.surface: An American composer, almost a person who captivates both sides of an audience.
explanation.walkthrough: BEING shortened to BEIN holds RL.
explanation.definitionFit: Irving Berlin was the Russian-born American songwriter of White Christmas and many Broadway hits.

clue.text: Malaysian city swamped by surplus vitality

indicators.note: something swamped is engulfed, so these letters sit inside the next word

parts.note: spare means surplus, extra to needs
KL is the usual short form of Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia's capital

explanation.surface: A Malaysian city overwhelmed by an excess of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: Malaysia's capital Kuala Lumpur is routinely shortened to its initials.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparkle is liveliness and brilliance in personality, a near synonym of vitality.

clue.text: Book, sale item gent returned in South-Western city

parts.note: B is short for book

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so these words are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a lot is an item in an auction sale
sir is a form of address for a gentleman

explanation.surface: A gentleman returns a book bought at a sale in a city in the west of England.
explanation.walkthrough: B followed by LOT and SIR read backwards, RISTOL.
explanation.definitionFit: Bristol is a major city in the South West region of England, on the River Avon.

clue.text: Significant attempt to suppress love, showing prejudice

indicators.note: to suppress is to hold down and keep in, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: big means significant or important
a try is an attempt
love is zero in tennis scores, written O

explanation.surface: A major effort to crush love, revealing intolerance.
explanation.walkthrough: BIG then TRY holding O: BIG + T(O)RY.
explanation.definitionFit: Bigotry is intolerance towards people of other views or groups, which is prejudice.

clue.text: Flower covering half of lake? That's probable

indicators.note: to cover is to go over and around, so the flower encloses the letters

parts.note: the lily is a flower

indicators.note: half of the word is kept, here its second pair of letters

parts.note: the back half of lake

explanation.surface: Water lilies spreading over half a lake, which seems quite possible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' could be a river in crosswords, but here it is simply a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Something likely is expected to happen, the same meaning as probable.

clue.text: Worthless sort initially dumped for reliable sort

indicators.note: the initial letter is dumped, thrown away, leaving the remainder

parts.note: a crock is a broken-down or useless person or thing

explanation.surface: Dropping a useless person in favour of a dependable one.
explanation.walkthrough: CROCK minus its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone a rock means they are steady and dependable, someone others lean on.

clue.text: Need to bracket anything Republican in sounds of hilarity

indicators.note: brackets enclose, so this word goes around the others

parts.note: a lack is a need or want

indicators.note: in places the second letter right after the first piece within the bracketed group

parts.note: aught is an old word for anything
R stands for Republican

explanation.surface: A need to enclose anything a Republican says in bursts of laughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Anything' is the old word aught, still met in phrases like 'for aught I know'.
explanation.definitionFit: A laugh track is recorded audience laughter added to a TV comedy, a soundtrack of mirth.

clue.text: Alert, as you'd expect the Marines to be?

parts.note: à la means in the manner of, as you would expect from
RM stands for the Royal Marines

explanation.surface: Marines are naturally on alert, as anyone would expect.
explanation.walkthrough: A LA (in the style of) plus RM: in the manner of the Marines.
explanation.definitionFit: An alarm is a warning signal, and as a verb to alert someone, so the two words match as nouns or verbs.

clue.text: Quantity of hair standing up on head of University tutor?

indicators.note: in a down answer, standing up means reading from bottom to top, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: rug is slang for a mass of hair, often a toupee

parts.note: the first letter of University

explanation.surface: A university tutor with hair standing up on end.
explanation.walkthrough: RUG read upwards gives GUR, followed by U.
explanation.definitionFit: A guru is a spiritual teacher or mentor, so a tutor in the broad sense of instructor.

clue.text: Repository of champagne: pour after formality?

indicators.note: after means coming later, so the second piece is placed behind the first

parts.note: ice is coldness of manner, a stiff formality
to bucket, or bucket down, is British for to pour with rain

explanation.surface: Pouring champagne once the formal speeches are over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pour' suggests serving the champagne; here it is rain, since 'bucket down' is British for pouring heavily.
explanation.definitionFit: Champagne is kept chilled in an ice bucket, a container filled with ice, so it is where the bottle is stored.

clue.text: Good storyteller held back object of quest

parts.note: G is short for good

indicators.note: held back suggests going backwards, so the word is read right to left

parts.note: a storyteller is someone who tells fibs, a liar

explanation.surface: A good storyteller holding back the climax of a quest tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Storyteller' is a euphemism for one who tells lies. G then LIAR backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The Holy Grail was the object sought by the knights of Arthurian legend, so any longed-for goal is a grail.

clue.text: Upset in tummy seems a response by this?

definitions.text: Upset in tummy seems a response by this?

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the anagram fodder, every letter used

explanation.surface: A stomach upset looks like the body's defences reacting to something.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: a tummy upset is a reaction the body's defences produce.
explanation.definitionFit: The immune system is the body's defence network, which responds to infections such as gut bugs.
